name: LeadTrack Entries for Contact Form 7
author: worldextechnologies

sections.description:
LeadTrack Entries for Contact Form 7 automatically saves every Contact Form 7 submission
to your WordPress database, along with a clean, modern admin dashboard to
browse, search, and export them – built and maintained by
WorldEx Technologies.

Features

  • No configuration needed – just activate
  • Saves every CF7 submission to a dedicated database table
  • Automatic Page URL tracking – know exactly which page each inquiry came from
  • Automatic Source tracking – Google, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Google/Facebook Ads, a UTM campaign, a referring site, or Direct
  • Clean, modern admin UI to browse entries per form
  • Search entries
  • Mark entries as read / unread
  • Bulk delete
  • Export entries to CSV (including Page URL and Source columns)
  • Developer friendly hooks and filters

Setting up Source tracking

Nothing to set up – Page URL and Source are both captured automatically
for every form on your site the moment you activate the plugin. It adds
its own tracking fields to each Contact Form 7 form behind the scenes
using Contact Form 7’s built-in hidden-fields filter, so there is no form
template to edit.

See DOCUMENTATION.txt in the plugin folder for details and developer hooks.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the leadtrack-entries-for-contact-form-7 folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Make sure Contact Form 7 is installed and active.
  4. Submissions will start appearing under “CF7 Entries” in the admin menu – Page URL and Source are tracked automatically, no extra setup required.
sections.faq:
Does Page URL or Source tracking need any setup?

No – both are captured automatically for every submission on every form as soon as the plugin is active.

Why does Source sometimes show “Direct” for a visitor I know came from Google?

This can happen if the visitor has JavaScript disabled in their browser. In that rare case the plugin falls back to a server-side guess, which is less precise for AJAX-submitted forms.
